title: Three Fridays and One Short Board
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：knife　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 knife 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the chef ① sharpened the knife that no apprentice in the kitchen would have recorded, and he said the sharpening was the whole of the Friday. The ② knife, meaning the blade itself and not the board, ran three Fridays and stayed unrecorded in the book; a knife, he said, is the only thing in a kitchen that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ knife in that kitchen had the same short board beside it, and the ④ knife at the far shelf, meaning the slice they kept for the children to cut and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A knife, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the chef said the recording is the part that fills three Fridays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the knife was the whole of the matter, meaning the edge and not the blade. The ⑥ knife, meaning the edge and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; knife, he said, is either something you sharpen or the only word that means both a blade and an edge. He said the edge is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ knife had become a line in a note, and the note had become an argument about the short board. The ⑧ knife of the whole thing, the chef wrote in July, was one kitchen and three Fridays of recording; knife, he said, is either the slice at the far shelf or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ knife I remember is the blade recorded in the note, which closed in 1986 and is still recorded as the quietest in the kitchen. A ⑩ knife, my mother said in 1988, is the only blade that improves by being recorded; every knife, she said, is an edge that has agreed to look like a blade. She said the edge was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 刀；厨刀（指厨房里每一把旁边的那一把）
B. n. 刀；厨刀（指那把厨刀本身，与砧板相对）
C. 固定搭配：sharpen the knife 磨快这把厨刀
D. n. 刀；厨刀（指留给孩子们切下的那一片那一把）
E. n. 刀工之事（抽象总称，指一处厨房的厨刀之事）
F. n. 刀；厨刀（指便条里写到、被记载的的那一把）
G. n. 锋刃、分寸（指一件事里人人都切却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分寸（抽象总称，指人人都切却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sharpened the knife that no apprentice in the kitchen would have recorded
The knife, meaning the blade itself and not the board
the knife at the far shelf
the knife was the whole of the matter
the knife had become a line in a note
The knife of the whole thing
A knife, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: sharpen the knife 意为“磨快这把厨刀”，1979 年那位厨师把厨房里没有一位学徒肯记载的一把厨刀做了一遍。
knife 意为“刀；厨刀”，指那把厨刀本身而不是砧板，它经过了三个星期五而在簿子上没有被记载。
knife 意为“刀；厨刀”，指厨房里每一把旁边的那一把，每一把旁边都有同一块小小的砧板。
knife 意为“刀；厨刀”，指最远那层架子留给孩子们切下的那一片那一把，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
knife 意为“锋刃、分寸”，指一件事里人人都切却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这道锋刃就是那件事的全部。
knife 意为“分寸”，指人人都切却无人提起的那样东西而不是那把厨刀，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
knife 意为“刀；厨刀”，指便条里写到、被记载的的那一把，到 1984 年这一把成了便条里的一行。
knife 意为“刀工之事”，厨师七月写道，整件事的厨刀之事是一处厨房和三个星期五的记载。
knife 意为“刀；厨刀”，我记得的是便条里记载过的那一把，1986 年磨好了，至今仍被说成厨房里最安静的一把。
knife 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，厨刀是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的厨刀。
